messages:
customer_jane: Hey team — since ~13:05 we've been getting 503s from Redwood hosted inference for several endpoints (mostly /v1/generate). Example request id: req_7b9f2c. Error in client: "upstream inference worker error (exit code 139)". Can you help?

sara (support): Sorry you're hitting this — I'm looking. Which model + region? Any recent config changes?

customer_jane: model=redwood-13b-qa-quant, region=us-west-2. No config changes on our side. We saw latency spike then failures.

deploy-bot: deploy service/hosted-infer version=2026.03.12-canary started by priy during 12:58 UTC

mike (infra): I'm pulling the worker logs now, seeing repeated container restarts on the gpupool in us-west-2. Sample from kube logs:
```
2026-03-12T13:06:07Z infer-runner[pid=42]: segfault (signal 11) at 0x00007ff...
2026-03-12T13:06:07Z kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4213 (infer-runner) total-vm:...
2026-03-12T13:06:07Z containerd: container exited with status 139
```
Also nvml shows ephemeral GPU memory spike followed by OOM.

priya (ml-eng): That can line up with the quantized runtime change we rolled to canary at 12:58 — it enabled aggressive kv-prefetch for long context. If kv prefetch doesn't respect per-request seq_len distribution it can spike GPU memory.

mike (infra): +1, I see the canary nodes running the new runtime. Crash pattern is OOM then segfault on allocation path.

tony (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) rollback canary to previous runtime on gpupool-usw2, 2) update routing to direct traffic to fallback-model small-embed for high-latency customers, 3) temporarily lower max_batch_size to 1 for that pool. I'll run the rollback now.

sara (support): @customer_jane doing 2/3 help reduce your impact — we'll confirm when 1 is done.

deploy-bot: rollback service/hosted-infer to version=2026.03.05-stable initiated by tony

tony (oncall): rollback completed at 13:12 UTC. Also reduced max_batch_size from 8 -> 1 on gpupool-usw2. Routing change pushed to send heavy traffic to us-east-1 fallback.

mike (infra): After rollback, node restart rate dropped and container exit codes stopped. Metrics: error_rate for /v1/generate went from 7.3% -> 0.6% in 10min. GPU mem spike graphs attached to incident board. :thumbsup:

customer_jane: Thanks — failures stopped for us after ~13:13. Appreciate the quick rollback.

priya (ml-eng): Root suspicion: kv-prefetch in the new quant-runtime bypassed per-request seq_len cap which allowed bad request patterns to allocate worst-case kv cache across batch. We'll reproduce locally and add a guard.

mike (infra): We'll also add a prometheus alert on per-node `gpu_reserved_memory` delta to catch this class earlier.

sara (support): I'm opening a follow-up ticket with the customer for status and next steps. We'll send an interim postmortem within 48h with timeline + remediation.

customer_jane: Good plan. Please cc me on the postmortem.

tony (oncall): noted. Assigning to priy + mike for RCA. Tagging incident P1 -> in progress. :eyes:

deploy-bot: incident P1 (2222222222) updated: status=in_progress assigned_to=[priya (ml-eng), mike (infra)]

mike (infra): Quick note for the record: observed one pod with exit_code=139 plus `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in its stderr prior to crash — consistent with memory corruption after OOM.

priya (ml-eng): Repro steps I'm running: replay logged request batch (req_7b9f2c) against quant-runtime with kv_prefetch enabled + seq_len flood; reproduces OOM locally within 30s. Will push a fix to clamp kv_prefetch and add unit test.

sara (support): Thanks team — I'll update customer_jane when RCA draft is ready.

customer_jane: Thanks everyone.
